newsitem.title: UK: British politician united with long-lost son.
newsitem.headline: British politician united with long-lost son.

text.p: A leading member of Britain's opposition Labour party was reunited with the son she gave up for adoption 31 years ago, newspapers said on Thursday.
Clare Short, Labour spokeswoman for overseas development, met her son, Toby Graham, a supporter of the ruling Conservative Party, four weeks ago.
The last time she saw him was when he was six weeks old.
"We are at the moment happier than we have been in our lives," Short and her son said in a joint statement. "It is more wonderful than anyone can image and makes both of us feel complete."

Short, a Roman Catholic, said in an interview with The Independent newspaper that she discovered she was pregnant shortly after her 18th birthday. She married the father, but because of financial problems she decided to give the boy up for adoption.
"When they came to take him it was terrible. It's been terrible ever since," she said.

But the story had a happy ending after Toby, a lawyer, began searching for his natural mother. In addition to finding her son, Short, who has since divorced and remarried, also discovered she has two grandchildren.
